final_report.summary: Successfully implemented localStorage persistence for the Mission Suggestions panel sort/filter state in the AtlasForge dashboard. The implementation persists sort field (currentSortField), sort direction (currentSortDirection), and tag filter (currentTagFilter) across page reloads using a single JSON blob stored under the key 'rec_sort_filter_state'. State is saved on every user interaction with sort/filter controls and restored on page load before the first render. The implementation includes defensive error handling (try/catch), validation of stored values against available DOM options, and graceful fallback to defaults when stored values are stale or invalid.
key_achievements: Implemented saveRecSortState() function that serializes sortField, sortDirection, and tagFilter to localStorage as a single JSON object under key 'rec_sort_filter_state'
Implemented loadRecSortState() function that restores all three values before first render, with DOM synchronization for sort select, sort direction button text, and tag filter select
Added validation: sort field value is only accepted if the corresponding <option> exists in the DOM (prevents stale values from breaking the UI)
Added validation: sort direction is only accepted if it is 'asc' or 'desc'
Tag filter (#rec-tag-filter) persistence fully integrated into the same state blob
Defensive error handling (try/catch) prevents localStorage quota errors or parse failures from breaking the dashboard
challenges_overcome: Earlier implementation attempt left a bare 'rec-tag' text as a JavaScript statement (syntax error at line 283) — replaced with proper implementation
Duplicate variable declarations (savedSortField2, savedSortDir2) from an earlier attempt were removed
DOM timing: loadRecSortState() correctly handles the case where the sort select element may not yet exist in the DOM by storing the value in the JS variable and letting the render function pick it up

Stale value handling: if a previously persisted sortField value no longer matches any option in the select element, the code resets to the current default rather than leaving the select in an inconsistent state
lessons_learned: Persisting multiple related filter/sort values as a single JSON blob (rather than individual localStorage keys) simplifies save/load logic and reduces key namespace pollution
Always validate restored values against the live DOM before applying them — stored enum values can become stale if the UI options change between versions
Wrap all localStorage operations in try/catch — browsers in private mode or with storage quotas exhausted will throw, and dashboard functionality must not break
Use a single named constant (REC_SORT_STORAGE_KEY) for the localStorage key to avoid typos and make future key changes trivial
